title: KT Signal Connector API v1 host frame

proxyGroupId.description: Proxy group identifier (ADR 0001, Phase 4). 'default' is the reserved, always-present group; additional groups are defined by the trusted launcher at connector spawn and are never created over IPC. An omitted proxyGroup means 'default'.

proxyGroup.description: Optional target proxy group for the account being linked; fixed for the life of the link once link.finish succeeds. An unknown group fails with PROXY_GROUP_NOT_FOUND. A pre-Phase-4 connector rejects this field with INVALID_REQUEST (deny_unknown_fields), so hosts must feature-detect via runtime.status first.

messagesSearchParams.description: Contract 1.30: account-wide substring search over stored message bodies. Empty or whitespace-only queries answer an empty page; queries over 128 characters are rejected (INVALID_REQUEST).

messagesSendTextParams.description: Exactly one addressing form must be set: conversationId, or kind+peerKey (peerTitle optional). mentions (contract revision 1.34) is the optional outbound @mention list: at most 64 entries (extras are dropped, the §4.20 receive cap mirrored); number resolves contacts-first with ACI/UUID passthrough — an entry whose number resolves to nothing local is dropped (the official behavior for unresolvable mention addresses), and an empty number fails closed INVALID_REQUEST; start/length are UTF-16 code-unit offsets the caller indexes against its own body (the official BodyRange semantics).

kind.description: Peer target kind; 'contact' and 'direct' both address a direct chat.

peerKey.description: Recipient number/uuid for direct chats, group id for groups.

peerTitle.description: Optional display title used when the peer send creates a new conversation.

text.description: Non-empty text; the service authoritatively enforces at most 65536 UTF-8 bytes.

number.description: The mentioned address: a phone number (resolved against the local contacts cache, digit-suffix rule) or a UUID-shaped ACI (passthrough).

start.description: UTF-16 code-unit offset into the caller's body.

length.description: UTF-16 code-unit length of the mentioned range.

messagesRetryTextParams.description: Contract 1.31: retry one definitively-failed outgoing text by its clientRequestId (the same idempotency key the original send used). The connector rearms the SAME pending row (status 'failed' -> 'pending') and re-dispatches the upstream send rebuilt from the persisted record — a retry never mints a new clientRequestId, so the local history keeps exactly one row per logical message (official resend behavior; the superseded-row duplication of a naive new-id retry cannot occur). Guards: the row must be an outgoing text with a stored clientRequestId in the terminal state 'failed' — 'pending' answers RETRY_IN_FLIGHT, 'unknown' answers RETRY_NOT_ALLOWED (its wire outcome was never settled, so a blind resend could double-deliver; the host must never auto-resend an unknown outcome), incoming/system rows and rows without a clientRequestId answer INVALID_REQUEST, a missing row or conversation answers MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND / CONVERSATION_NOT_FOUND. Settlement follows messages.sendText: the response is the SAME MessageRecord (same row id) now 'sent', an indeterminate outcome answers SEND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN leaving the row 'unknown', a definite upstream error answers UPSTREAM_ERROR with the row back in 'failed'.

query.description: Optional case-insensitive substring filter over title and peerKey; read-only over the local cache.

messagesEditParams.description: Edit one message the linked account itself sent (contract 1.15). Only a local outgoing row in the terminal state 'sent' qualifies: its sentAt is the upstream Signal timestamp the edit targets via editTimestamp; pending/failed/unknown rows carry no protocol identity and answer MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND. Dispatches signal-cli send with editTimestamp; the connector enforces no local edit window — a late edit answers the upstream rejection (UPSTREAM_ERROR). On confirmed success the updated MessageRecord is returned (body replaced, editedAt set, status unchanged); when the outcome of the mutating upstream call cannot be determined the answer is SEND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and the local row is unchanged; 'unknown' is never retried automatically by the connector. Targeting is by conversationId only — the target must already exist in the local history. clientRequestId is accepted for host correlation but the connector does not persist it for edits.

text.description: New message body; bounds identical to messages.sendText.

clientRequestId.description: Optional host correlation id; validated but not persisted.

messagesRemoteDeleteParams.description: Remotely delete (Delete for everyone) one message the linked account itself sent. Only a local outgoing row in the terminal state 'sent' qualifies: its sentAt is the upstream Signal timestamp addressed by the delete; pending/failed/unknown rows carry no protocol identity and answer MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND. Best effort upstream semantics (24h window, quoted/replying messages are not removed). Targeting is by conversationId only — the target must already exist in the local history. The result is {status: 'deleted'} when signal-cli confirmed the delete, or {status: 'unknown'} when the outcome of the mutating upstream call cannot be determined; 'unknown' is never retried automatically by the connector (host may explicitly re-send with a fresh requestId and the same operationId). operationId is an optional host correlation id; the connector validates its shape but does not persist it.

messagesSendReactionParams.description: Send or remove a reaction to one message that already exists in the local history. Targeting is by conversationId only. A local outgoing row qualifies in the terminal state 'sent' (its sentAt is the upstream Signal timestamp); an incoming row carries the envelope timestamp, so both directions are addressable. The target author follows the row direction: the linked account's own number for outgoing rows, the conversation peer for incoming rows. Rows without a resolvable protocol identity (missing, pending/failed/unknown outgoing, system) answer MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND; a group incoming row persists only a local sender hash, so its author is not resolvable and the request fails with a deterministic INVALID_REQUEST. The result is {status: 'sent'} when signal-cli confirmed the reaction, or {status: 'unknown'} when the outcome of the mutating upstream call cannot be determined; 'unknown' is never retried automatically by the connector (host may explicitly re-send with a fresh requestId and the same operationId). operationId is an optional host correlation id; the connector validates its shape but does not persist it. remove=true removes a previously sent reaction (upstream best effort).

emoji.description: The reaction; a single unicode grapheme cluster of at most 32 UTF-8 bytes, mirroring the pinned signal-cli requirement.

remove.description: True removes a previously sent reaction; the emoji must still identify the reaction to remove.

messagesSendPinMessageParams.description: Pin one message that already exists in the local history (contract revision 1.33; one pinned message per conversation, the official model). Addressing follows the messages.sendReaction model: a local outgoing row qualifies in the terminal state 'sent' (its sentAt is the upstream Signal timestamp); an incoming direct row carries the envelope timestamp; the target author follows the row direction (the linked account's own number for outgoing rows, the conversation peer for incoming direct rows). Rows without a resolvable protocol identity (missing, pending/failed/unknown outgoing, system, group incoming — only a local sender hash is persisted) fail closed: MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND or a deterministic INVALID_REQUEST. Groups address the engine groupId form, direct chats the recipient array. pinDurationSeconds is the optional timed-pin duration: absent or null is the official forever pin, and a value outside 0..4294967295 fails closed with INVALID_REQUEST. The result is {status: 'sent'} when the upstream confirmed the pin, or {status: 'unknown'} when the outcome of the mutating upstream call cannot be determined; 'unknown' is never retried automatically by the connector (host may explicitly re-send with a fresh requestId and the same operationId). operationId is an optional host correlation id; the connector validates its shape but does not persist it.

pinDurationSeconds.description: Optional timed-pin duration in seconds; absent or null means the pin never expires.

messagesSendUnpinMessageParams.description: Unpin one message that already exists in the local history (contract revision 1.33). Same addressing as messages.sendPinMessage, with no duration: the official unpinMessage carries only the target identity. The result is {status: 'sent'} when the upstream confirmed the unpin, or {status: 'unknown'} when the outcome of the mutating upstream call cannot be determined; 'unknown' is never retried automatically by the connector (host may explicitly re-send with a fresh requestId and the same operationId). operationId is an optional host correlation id; the connector validates its shape but does not persist it.

messagesSendAdminDeleteParams.description: Remove one message from a group conversation as a group admin (contract revision 1.33; the official deleted-by-admin tombstone). Direct chats have no admin concept and answer INVALID_REQUEST before any upstream call. Same addressing as messages.sendPinMessage; admin eligibility is not pre-checked — the server is the authority and rejects non-admin attempts, which surface as the upstream error. A group incoming row persists only a local sender hash, so its author is not resolvable and the request fails with a deterministic INVALID_REQUEST. The result is {status: 'sent'} when the upstream confirmed the removal, or {status: 'unknown'} when the outcome of the mutating upstream call cannot be determined; 'unknown' is never retried automatically by the connector (host may explicitly re-send with a fresh requestId and the same operationId). operationId is an optional host correlation id; the connector validates its shape but does not persist it.

messagesMarkReadParams.description: Send the upstream read receipt for messages the peers authored (contract revision 1.34; official sendReceipts per-author fan-out, one engine sendReadReceipt per author with that author's timestamps, the engine chunking 100 per envelope). messageIds is optional: absent means every incoming row of the conversation in ascending sentAt order, both forms bounded at 512 (an explicit list beyond 512 is truncated, not rejected). Only incoming rows qualify — outgoing and system rows are skipped; rows whose author cannot be resolved from local data (group rows carry only a local sender hash) are skipped from the fan-out, not an error. The connector does not persist our own read state (the desktop owns its unread state), so the absent form may re-receipt rows the desktop already marked — duplicates are protocol-idempotent for the peer. The result is {status: 'sent'} when every per-author upstream call confirmed, or {status: 'unknown'} when any failed (including an indeterminate outcome); a receipt failure never fails the request and 'unknown' is never retried automatically. Zero eligible rows is a trivial {status: 'sent'} no-op.

messageIds.description: Optional explicit selection; only incoming rows of this conversation qualify, others are skipped.

messagesMarkViewedParams.description: Send the upstream viewed receipt (contract revision 1.34): identical addressing, selection bounds, per-author fan-out, and {status: sent|unknown} aggregation as messages.markRead, with the engine sendViewedReceipt upstream face.

messageIds.description: Optional explicit selection; only incoming rows of this conversation qualify, others are skipped.

messagesSendViewOnceOpenParams.description: Forward the official view-once open notification (contract revision 1.38): the engine sendViewOnceOpen {account, senderAci, timestamp} face verbatim. Bare passthrough — the desktop flow does not call this directly (messages.markViewOnceOpened orchestrates both legs of the official order); result is receipt-class {status: sent|unknown} and failures degrade to unknown without retry.

timestamp.description: The viewed message's upstream timestamp (ms); 0 carries the official unknown-marker semantics.

messagesMarkViewOnceOpenedParams.description: Burn a viewed view-once message (contract revision 1.38): erase the row body bytes and the connector-owned media files, close open media handles, downgrade the row projection to the viewed placeholder, emit message.viewOnceOpened once, then best-effort orchestrate the official upstream pair (sendViewedReceipt to the author, then sendViewOnceOpen) under receipt-class discipline — failures degrade and are never retried, the burn and the event are unaffected. The desktop's single trigger point for the view-once flow; calling messages.markViewed / messages.sendViewOnceOpen separately is unnecessary (protocol-idempotent if it happens).

messagesAttachmentsOpenParams.description: Open a chunked stream for one already-downloaded attachment (ADR 0002, contract revision 1.17). The (accountId, conversationId, messageId) triple resolves against the store before any file is touched — a bogus conversation or message answers CONVERSATION_NOT_FOUND / MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND. The attachmentId must be a bare file name (the id field of the received message's attachment metadata): any id containing '/' or '\\', or any id that resolves to '' / '.' / '..' under the upstream sanitizeId transform ([^A-Za-z0-9_.-] replaced by '_'), answers INVALID_REQUEST before the filesystem is touched, so a hostile id cannot path-traverse. A file signal-cli has not downloaded — or that the media governor already deleted — answers UPSTREAM_ERROR; the two are deliberately indistinguishable. Without the launcher-level --media-ingest opt-in every media method answers CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE. The response is {mediaHandle, sizeBytes, chunkBytes}: mediaHandle is an unguessable 128-bit token bound to this resolved tuple (300 s TTL, at most 8 live handles per account, released early by messages.attachments.closeHandle), sizeBytes is the locally measured file size, and chunkBytes is the raw chunk size (262144) every readChunk offset advances by.

attachmentId.description: The upstream attachment id from the received message's attachment metadata; a bare file name, never a path.

messagesAttachmentsReadChunkParams.description: Read the next chunk of a stream opened with messages.attachments.open (ADR 0002). Offsets are strictly sequential — offset must equal the number of bytes already delivered on this handle — so a handle can never become a random-access scan oracle; any other offset answers INVALID_REQUEST. The response is {dataBase64, sizeBytes, eof}: sizeBytes counts this chunk's raw bytes (at most chunkBytes = 262144; dataBase64 is its padded standard base64, at most 4 * ceil(262144 / 3) = 349528 characters, bounded and far inside the 160 MiB host frame budget) and eof terminates the caller's read loop. A closed, expired, or unknown handle answers INVALID_REQUEST; a file truncated under the stream (media governor pass) terminates with a short chunk and eof; a file that vanished entirely answers UPSTREAM_ERROR.

offset.description: Must equal the bytes already read on this handle; 0 for the first read.

messagesAttachmentsCloseHandleParams.description: Release a media stream before its 300 s TTL (ADR 0002). Idempotent: the response is {released}, false when the handle was already gone (expired or closed earlier). Handles are also released when their account's local data is deleted; the TTL backstops every other kind of abandonment.

messagesSendAttachmentParams.description: Exactly one addressing form must be set: conversationId, or kind+peerKey (peerTitle optional). Sends one attachment (contract revision 1.13, budget raised to the official 100 MiB ceiling in 1.16): dataBase64 is standard padded base64 whose decoded size must equal sizeBytes (1..104857600 bytes, the official Signal attachment ceiling). The connector re-encodes the payload as an RFC 2397 data URI for the upstream send call and never persists attachment bytes. Optional filename (1..128 bytes, no path separators or control characters) and contentType (type/subtype) become data-URI parameters; text is an optional caption subject to the sendText byte bound. voiceNote (contract revision 1.35) marks the attachment as a voice note: the data URI gains the ;voice=true parameter the engine maps to the official VOICE_MESSAGE flag, and the sent row's descriptor carries isVoiceNote — voiceNote requires contentType audio/* and is rejected INVALID_REQUEST before the pending row exists. Settlement follows messages.sendText: the response is the sent MessageRecord, and an indeterminate mutating outcome answers SEND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN with no automatic retry.

kind.description: Peer target kind; 'contact' and 'direct' both address a direct chat.

peerKey.description: Recipient number/uuid for direct chats, group id for groups.

peerTitle.description: Optional display title used when the peer send creates a new conversation.

dataBase64.description: Standard padded base64 of the attachment bytes; decoded size must equal sizeBytes. The bound is 4 * ceil(104857600 / 3) — the exact padded-base64 length for the 100 MiB ceiling.

sizeBytes.description: Declared raw attachment size; verified against the decoded payload before anything is sent.

filename.description: Optional display filename for the data URI; path separators and control characters are rejected.

contentType.description: Optional RFC 2045 media type 'type/subtype'; defaults to application/octet-stream.

text.description: Optional caption; the service authoritatively enforces at most 65536 UTF-8 bytes.

voiceNote.description: Send the attachment as a voice note (contract revision 1.35): the data URI gains ;voice=true (engine maps it to the official VOICE_MESSAGE flag — the exact wire shape the official desktop recorder emits) and the sent descriptor records isVoiceNote. Requires contentType audio/*; anything else is INVALID_REQUEST before the pending row exists.

viewOnce.description: Send the attachment as a view-once message (contract revision 1.38): the upstream send carries viewOnce=true and the sent row's rich record carries viewOnce so the sender's bubble renders the burn UI across restarts. Requires contentType image/* or video/*, an empty caption, no quoteMessageId, and no voiceNote; any violation is INVALID_REQUEST before the pending row exists.

messagesSendStickerParams.description: Exactly one addressing form must be set: conversationId, or kind+peerKey (peerTitle optional). Sends one sticker (contract revision 1.35, mirroring the official sendStickerMessage face): packId is the official hex pack id (even length, 1-64 characters), packKey the standard-base64 pack key (1-128 characters), stickerId the pack-local id, emoji an optional ≤32-character label. image follows the messages.attachments.send budget family (dataBase64 standard padded base64, decoded size must equal sizeBytes, 1..104857600 bytes) with one sticker-specific rule: contentType must be image/* (the official client sniffs image MIME and refuses video/text). The upstream send carries only the sticker object — no message body, no regular attachments. The optional quoteMessageId (contract revision 1.37, §4.35) quotes one message in the same conversation: one upstream send carries the sticker object and the quote identity together (the official StagedStickerReply shape); settlement discipline is unchanged. Settlement follows messages.sendText: the response is the sent MessageRecord whose descriptor records the sticker image plus the pack identity, and an indeterminate mutating outcome answers SEND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN with no automatic retry.

kind.description: Peer target kind; 'contact' and 'direct' both address a direct chat.

peerKey.description: Recipient number/uuid for direct chats, group id for groups.

peerTitle.description: Optional display title used when the peer send creates a new conversation.

quoteMessageId.description: Optional message to quote (contract revision 1.37, §4.35): resolves through the same ladder as messages.sendText — MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND for an unknown id, INVALID_REQUEST when the quoted author is not resolvable — and the upstream send carries quoteTimestamp/quoteAuthor beside the sticker object (the official StagedStickerReply shape). Absent means an unquoted sticker (the 1.35 behavior).

packId.description: Sticker pack id as the official client serializes it: hex, even length (each byte two hex chars), 1-64 characters; passed through verbatim after shape validation.

packKey.description: Sticker pack key in standard base64 (Bytes.fromBase64 convention), 1-128 characters; passed through verbatim after shape validation.

emoji.description: Optional emoji label for the sticker, at most 32 characters.

dataBase64.description: Standard padded base64 of the sticker image bytes; decoded size must equal sizeBytes. The bound is 4 * ceil(104857600 / 3) — the exact padded-base64 length for the 100 MiB ceiling.

sizeBytes.description: Declared raw image size; verified against the decoded payload before anything is sent.

contentType.description: RFC 2045 media type 'type/subtype'; must be image/* (the official client sniffs image MIME and refuses video/text).

width.description: Optional display width, passed through as official AttachmentPointer display metadata.

height.description: Optional display height, passed through as official AttachmentPointer display metadata.

stickerPackManifestParams.description: Fetch one sticker pack's manifest (contract revision 1.36, §4.32): the engine performs the anonymous CDN GET and the official decrypt pipeline (WebAPI.preload.ts fetch, Crypto.node.ts HKDF 'Sticker Pack' → AES-256-CBC+HMAC) — the connector never touches key material beyond passing packKey through, and never persists either field. packId is exactly 32 hex characters (official isPackIdValid — stricter than the 1.35 send projection's ≤64 on purpose); packKey is standard base64 decoding to exactly 32 bytes. Read lane, no account context, no local state. Structured engine errors: STICKER_PACK_KEY_INVALID / STICKER_PACK_FETCH_FAILED / STICKER_PACK_MALFORMED.

packId.description: Sticker pack id, exactly 32 hex characters (official isPackIdValid).

packKey.description: Standard padded base64 of the 32-byte pack key: exactly 44 characters (11 base64 groups, one '=' pad — the only padded encoding whose decode is exactly 32 bytes).

stickerPackImageParams.description: Fetch one sticker's decrypted bytes (contract revision 1.36, §4.32): same pack identity rules as stickerPacks.getManifest plus the pack-local stickerId. The result is {dataBase64, contentType, size} — the decrypted image as standard base64 (≤ 409600 chars: the official 300 KB CDN ceiling plus base64 expansion), its media type, and the decoded byte count. The bytes exist only inside the engine and the response; nothing is persisted. Structured engine errors: the manifest family plus STICKER_IMAGE_TOO_LARGE.

packId.description: Sticker pack id, exactly 32 hex characters (official isPackIdValid).

packKey.description: Standard padded base64 of the 32-byte pack key: exactly 44 characters.

conversationsGetPinnedParams.description: Read the account's pinned conversations (contract revision 1.36, §4.33): the engine reads the official Storage Service AccountRecord.pinnedConversations and the result projects {pinned: [{conversationId, kind}]} in cloud order — array order is the pin order, there are no timestamps. Read lane. The connector persists nothing: the host pulls at startup/refresh (poll-on-open, no live push on this face).

conversationsSetPinnedParams.description: Pin or unpin one conversation (contract revision 1.36, §4.33): the engine writes the official storage record (the same path the official desktop uses). conversationId resolves through the local store (CONVERSATION_NOT_FOUND before any upstream call); the result is the post-write cloud state {pinned: [...]} read back — not a local echo. Send lane, account-scoped mutating: an indeterminate outcome answers SEND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and is never retried. Structured engine errors: CONVERSATION_NOT_RESOLVED (the cloud reference does not resolve) and the STORAGE_* family passed through verbatim. Message-level pins (messages.sendPinMessage, §4.28) are an orthogonal concept — this face pins conversations, not messages.

conversationId.description: The conversation to pin or unpin; wider than the opaqueId family because the host may address a conversation not yet materialized locally. Resolved against the account before any upstream call.

kind.description: The upstream conversation reference taxonomy: direct chat, GroupsV2 group, or GroupsV1 legacy group.

pinned.description: true pins the conversation, false unpins it. Required — there is no toggle form.

stickerPackGetSyncsParams.description: Read the account's sticker-pack sync records (contract revision 1.37, §4.34): the engine reads the official Storage Service StickerPackRecord set — installed packs carry packId + packKey + position, uninstalled packs a deletedAtTimestampMs tombstone. The result projects {packs: [...]} in cloud order, capped at 256 entries (KT bound, overflow truncated, entries missing packId dropped). Read lane; the connector persists nothing — the cloud record plus the desktop's own cache is the whole story.

stickerPackSetSyncParams.description: Install or uninstall one sticker pack for the account (contract revision 1.37, §4.34): installed=true requires packKey (standard base64 decoding to exactly 32 bytes) and optionally positions the pack; installed=false writes the deletedAtTimestampMs tombstone and ignores packKey/position. The result is the post-write cloud state {packs: [...]} read back — not a local echo. Send lane, account-scoped mutating: an indeterminate outcome answers SEND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and is never retried. Structured engine errors: the STORAGE_* family passed through verbatim (retryable); no new codes are introduced by this face.

packId.description: Sticker pack id, exactly 32 hex characters (the §4.32 browse-face shape, aligned with the official isPackIdValid).

packKey.description: Pack key in standard base64 decoding to exactly 32 bytes (44 padded characters); required when installed is true, ignored (forwarded as null) otherwise.

installed.description: true installs the pack (packKey required), false uninstalls it (tombstone write). Required — there is no toggle form.

position.description: Optional cloud ordering position for an installed pack; u32 range. Ignored when installed is false.

groupsGetParams.description: Read-only projection (contract revision 1.9) of the local contacts cache for one group: {peerKey, title, memberCount?, syncedAt}. Served entirely from the rows written by contacts.sync — the connector never calls the upstream for this method, so an unsynced or departed group (the sync filters isMember=false) answers GROUP_NOT_FOUND; syncedAt lets the host judge staleness itself. Metrics classify it as contacts; no event is emitted.

groupKey.description: The upstream group id, exactly the peerKey of the cached kind='group' contacts row.

contactsSetLocalAliasParams.description: Rename one contact as the linked account sees it (contract revision 1.10): the mutating upstream updateContact carries {account, recipient, name}, where recipient is the peer key as a single string (the pinned UpdateContactCommand reads it with getString — an array would fail upstream). peerKey must resolve to a locally known contact (a cached kind='contact' row or a direct conversation peer); anything else answers INVALID_REQUEST. The result is {status: 'updated'} when signal-cli confirmed the rename, or {status: 'unknown'} when the outcome of the mutating upstream call cannot be determined; 'unknown' is never retried automatically by the connector (host may explicitly re-send with a fresh requestId and the same operationId). operationId is an optional host correlation id; the connector validates its shape but does not persist it. No local row is modified: the alias lives in upstream account data and returns through the next contacts.sync; no event is emitted.

peerKey.description: The contact's number/uuid; must already be known to this account.

alias.description: The new display name, at most 128 UTF-8 bytes.

presenceSetTypingMessageParams.description: Send or stop the typing indicator to one conversation (contract revision 1.11). The mutating upstream sendTyping command carries {account, stop, recipient: [peerKey]} for direct conversations or {account, stop, groupId} for groups; the connector always sends the stop boolean explicitly (the null handling of an absent key is not part of the pinned upstream contract), and signal-cli expires the indicator by itself after roughly 15 seconds, so stop=true is an early clear, not a requirement. Targeting is by conversationId only; a missing conversation row answers CONVERSATION_NOT_FOUND. The result is {status: 'sent'} when signal-cli confirmed the call, or {status: 'unknown'} when the outcome of the mutating upstream call cannot be determined; 'unknown' is never retried automatically by the connector (host may explicitly re-send with a fresh requestId and the same operationId). operationId is an optional host correlation id; the connector validates its shape but does not persist it. Nothing is written locally and no event is emitted: a typing indicator is ephemeral upstream protocol state, and inbound typing events remain a declared TODO.

stop.description: true stops an active indicator early; false (default) starts one.

historyImportStatusParams.description: Link-time history import status (contract revision 1.39, §4.38): the honest minimal projection of the backup5 archive import (ADR 0005 S3) for the desktop's S4 UI. Read-only over local state — it never touches the engine or the network. States: 'pending' (linked inside the link-time wait window, the engine's best-effort archive download has not produced the archive file yet), 'running'/'completed'/'failed' (from the persisted import row with real counters), 'unavailable' with reason 'engine-mode' (signal-cli JVM/native has no backup5 capability) or 'no-archive' (wait window expired with no archive — the engine's failure modes are indistinguishable from 'the phone had nothing to transfer' and are reported as such, never guessed). The desktop polls while state is 'running'; there is deliberately no push event in this revision.

groupId.description: Group whose engine sampled the pressure transition; 'default' in single-group deployments (ADR 0001).

data.description: One proxy group's engine transition (ADR 0001). runtime.stateChanged keeps carrying the top-level aggregate; this event carries per-group detail.
Ephemeral typing indicator (contract 1.15): never persisted, rate limited per account+conversation before it reaches the host lane. The host owns display timeout.

action.description: Upstream typingMessage action; START shows the indicator, STOP clears it immediately.

status.description: State one outgoing message transitioned to; emitted only on a real transition (pending -> sent/unknown/failed, receipts -> delivered/read), never replayed.

deliveredAt.description: Contract 1.32: connector wall-clock ms the delivery receipt that triggered this event stamped the row. Absent on transitions that did not stamp it.

readAt.description: Contract 1.32: connector wall-clock ms the read/viewed receipt that triggered this event stamped the row. Absent on transitions that did not stamp it.

data.description: A view-once message was viewed and its bytes erased (contract 1.38): the body is gone, the media files are deleted, and the row renders as the viewed placeholder. Emitted exactly once per message on the first burn transition — sync-envelope duplicates and replays emit nothing. Deliberately not a message.statusChanged payload: this is the local viewed state, not a peer receipt.

openedAt.description: Connector wall-clock ms the burn stamped the row.
